one_line: Frontier commander of the Delhi Sultanate who earned renown defending Dipalpur and Multan against repeated Mongol raids in the early 14th century.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, tall and broad-shouldered with a seasoned soldier’s build.
appearance.face: Oval face with a strong jaw, wheat-brown North Indian complexion, slightly sharp cheekbones hinting at mixed Mongol-Jat heritage, thin arched eyebrows, steady narrow dark eyes, trimmed mustache with a short pointed beard; default expression calm, alert and resolute.
appearance.hair: Straight, thick black hair to just below the ears, usually hidden beneath a padded quilted coif and a conical steel helmet with a small nasal bar and a plain brown leather chin strap.
appearance.costume: Over a long-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton tunic and loose brown cotton trousers, he wears a sleeveless mail-and-plate coat (brigandine) of dull steel with small rivet dots over a deep indigo quilted gambeson, secured with a plain brown leather belt; a practical dark-olive wool cloak hangs from his shoulders for frontier cold, and his feet are in dark-brown leather boots with slightly upturned toes; minimal jewellery, just a simple iron ring on his right hand, and a narrow deep-red cloth sash at his waist adds a subtle touch of colour.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved, single-edged Indo-Turkic sword (early talwar) with a steel blade, simple iron crossguard, and a brown leather-wrapped hilt, worn at his left hip in a plain dark-brown scabbard, which he often rests his right hand on when standing.

ref_desc: Ghazi Malik is a mid-30s tall, broad-shouldered frontier commander with wheat-brown skin, sharp dark eyes, a trimmed mustache and short pointed beard, straight black hair under a conical steel helmet, wearing an off-white tunic, brown trousers, deep indigo quilted gambeson beneath a dull-steel mail-and-plate coat, dark-olive cloak, brown leather boots and belt, and carrying a slightly curved Indo-Turkic sword in a brown scabbard at his left hip.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Ghazi Malik, a mid-30s tall, broad-shouldered frontier commander of the early 14th-century Delhi Sultanate, with an oval face, wheat-brown complexion, sharp cheekbones, steady narrow dark eyes, and a trimmed mustache with a short pointed beard, his straight black hair mostly hidden under a padded coif and a simple conical steel helmet with a nasal bar and leather chin strap; dress him in an off-white long-sleeved cotton tunic, loose brown trousers, a deep indigo quilted gambeson, and over that a sleeveless dull-steel mail-and-plate coat (brigandine) dotted with small rivets, cinched by a plain brown leather belt with a narrow deep-red cloth sash; add a dark-olive wool cloak draped from his shoulders, dark-brown leather boots with slightly upturned toes, and a simple iron ring on his right hand; his signature slightly curved Indo-Turkic sword with steel blade, plain iron crossguard, and brown leather-wrapped hilt hangs in a dark-brown scabbard at his left hip, his right hand resting lightly on the hilt; use a muted palette of deep indigo, dark olive green, off-white, brown leather, and dull steel grey, and show him from multiple angles to capture the consistent face, helmet, armor, cloak, boots, and sword details.
